studies.finding: Antisocial punishment varies across pools. The main text reports at least weakly significant punishment-associated contribution gains in eleven pools and no significant gain in five; more antisocial punishment is associated with weaker contribution gains, not a universal zero effect.
limitations: The author-institution metadata and selected published main text were read from the six-page PDF publicly linked by author Christian Thöni at https://people.unil.ch/christianthoeni/list-of-publications/ (Google Drive file 1mxpaP4N3VQe5QBQvD_17MTKADFaBxunG), with local OCR assistance. Supporting Methods/tables, treatment order/counterbalancing, raw data and regression calculations were not independently checked. The 1120 university undergraduates in sixteen participant pools are not national representative samples. Antisocial means punishing someone contributing at least as much as the punisher; behavior does not uniquely identify revenge, dominance or other motives.
The five nonsignificant contrasts are not equivalence tests or proof of exactly no benefit. Pool variation and punishment-behavior regressions are not randomized cultural mechanisms.

Fixed-group dependence, paired condition histories and unread treatment order prevent treating every round or condition as an independent experiment. Punishment motives are proposed explanations, not experimentally isolated mediators.

limitations: Main methods, results, figures and discussion were read in the university-hosted primary PDF. Electronic supplementary material and original observations remain unread/unreplayed. Male fasting was stopped when removal coincided with increased aggression. Mouth-licking duration proxies transfer and correlates with mass gain; partner-help predictors were not randomly assigned. A predictive association does not uniquely identify calculated reciprocity, enforcement or fitness benefit.

limitations: The main scientific text and displayed tables/figure legends were read through Europe PMC XML. Original tracking, chromatograms and code available on request were not replayed. Methods state 9 ng hydrocarbon per ant whereas Results state 9 microgram; this unresolved unit conflict prevents calibrated dose or receptor-threshold inference. Odor treatments and controls share a field-colony design, whereas the vestibule experiment uses two other colony observations with blanks preceding combined cues. The contemporary ant studies share investigators, species and field setting; complete cohort/data independence across papers was not established. Nonsignificant single-cue effects are finite nulls, not equivalence or proof of an absolute chemical necessity.
Both cue-class identity and mimic handling are part of the preparation; the unresolved hydrocarbon-unit conflict prevents a calibrated dose-response or minimum-signal rule.
